evidence: Three independent registration responses returned HTTP 200
Each cookie session returned its own account from GET /api/auth/me
Founder invited Member A and Member B
Both members retrieved pending invitations and accepted them
Organization detail showed all three stable account IDs as active members

journeys.finding: Accepting an organization invitation did not automatically make the account a project member. Founder had to POST /api/projects/{project_id}/members for each member before project messages exposed them.
evidence: Before explicit project-member addition, Member A project messages listed Founder only
After explicit addition, Member A saw Founder, Member A, and Member B

journeys.finding: Unauthenticated GET /api/projects/{project_id}/timeline returned HTTP 200 and an empty events list for the sandbox project. Unauthenticated project message write returned HTTP 401.
journeys.scope: The read boundary may be intentionally public or may be a journey/privacy defect; requires product decision and authenticated outsider test.

journeys.finding: GET /api/projects/{project_id}/members returned HTTP 405. The available route is POST for adding members; project member reads are embedded in project/message responses rather than exposed at that path.
